text:
zoe: FYI I hit a confusing combo of issues in VSCode Interactive. Pasted quickstart into the interactive window and got a RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'AsyncClient.chat.completions.create' was never awaited. The editor autocompletion showed it as a regular method so I didn't realize I needed `await`.

matt: ouch. Is the signature wrong in the stubs?

zoe: looks that way. mypy/pyright both infer the method as returning Any (no coroutine type) so completion hides the need to await. snippet I ran:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
resp = client.chat.completions.create(model="rwd-1", input="hey")
print(resp)
```

jana: we intentionally have both sync helpers and async client classes which probably made the typed stubs messy. The async methods should be typed as returning Coroutine[...] or an Awaitable. If the typing is Any, editors will treat it as already resolved.

rachel: also interactive windows and notebooks sometimes swallow RuntimeWarnings so people won't notice until they hit a downstream error. We should make the types explicit and maybe add runtime guards that raise a helpful error if a coroutine is used without await in interactive environments. Example error: "It looks like you're calling an async method from a running event loop — use `await` or `async with AsyncClient()`".

matt: small repro: in VSCode, with Pyright, the completion shows create(...) -> Any. If we publish proper .pyi stubs or inline typing that'll fix autocompletion. We should add tests that assert `inspect.iscoroutinefunction` for those methods.

zoe: filed GH issue #1967: "Python SDK: AsyncClient method typing and Interactive Window coroutine warnings" with a minimal sample and screenshots.

jana: proposed fixes: 1) update typings (.pyi or pyproject) so async client methods have precise Awaitable/Coroutine types, 2) add an editor-friendly note in Quickstart about "async vs sync" and a tiny snippet for VSCode Interactive/REPL, 3) add a runtime check when a method is called outside a running loop to suggest correct usage (but keep it opt-in / non-breaking).

type-bot: created task T-431: "Add typing for AsyncClient methods + runtime UX checks" and linked issue #1967.

matt: I'll draft the typing patch (pyi) and a unit test. Can someone add the Quickstart note?

rachel: putting a short blurb in docs this sprint. Also adding a small smoke check for Interactive window in our DX checklist.

zoe: thanks all — this would have saved me 20 minutes of head-scratching. I'll validate the patch when it's up. :thumbsup:
